grades.reason: Shows the RISC-V F-extension FMV.X.W and FMV.W.X encodings, which are the instructions that move single-precision bits between integer and FP registers. It doesn't state their semantics, and the rationale only covers why moves are less often needed.

grades.quote: FMV.X.H and FMV.H.X do not modify the bits being transferred; in particular, the payloads of noncanonical NaNs are preserved.
grades.reason: Directly explains FMV.X.H and FMV.H.X, which move half-precision bit patterns between FP and integer registers. It covers sign-fill, NaN-boxing, and the fact that the bits are not modified.

grades.quote: FMV.X.Q and FMV.Q.X instructions are not provided in RV32 or RV64, so quad-precision bit patterns must be moved to the integer registers via memory.
grades.reason: Says that the quad-precision raw-bit move instructions are not provided in RV32 or RV64, so values must go through memory. This is limited auxiliary information, since it names the instructions but only to say they don't exist.
